notes: Method: every item's full thread read in date order to the last message; all twelve evidence_quote strings machine-verified as exact substrings of the cited message's body_text or attachment extracted_text (12/12 pass, item 03 correctly resolving into the PDF's extracted_text). No double counting found — the three Lumenpay legal documents (MSA amendment / security addendum / DPA addendum) are genuinely distinct instruments, and no thread yields two items. All eight distractors survive scrutiny and none should be promoted: payroll really was approved (a10f18c2e4b60049 'Approved — go ahead'), the diffused SOC2 ask really was claimed by Luis 47 minutes later (a60f18c2e4b60024 position 2, 'I'll grab this'), and the Stripe dispute really is Wendy's (meta.action_owner = wendy@kettlehq.com). Two smaller observations that did not rise to findings: (a) founder-q1-04 carries due_date 2026-07-03 while its anchor is the Aug 7 envelope — defensible as obligation-origin dating, but the 'overdue by nearly six weeks' phrasing understates that the stated condition (Beth's sign-off) was demonstrably still unmet on Jul 22 per a60f18c2e4b60020, so the honest framing is a conditional promise whose condition resolved late, not a flatly blown deadline; (b) founder-q1-12 versus a10f18c2e4b60042, where Sana tells Greg at 16:50 on Aug 6 'it'll be a live agenda item, not a written consent' — 80 minutes after the written-consent envelope went out at 15:30. Most likely two different instruments (an immediate 800K-share consent for the Naomi Chen offer versus the broader 8% refresh discussion), but a human reviewer should confirm the corpus intends that reading. Finally, the corpus contains two audit firms running what reads like one SOC2 Type II (Certiva/Rachel Kim and Vantage/Owen Fitch then Grace Liu) with incompatible schedules — Aug 13 evidence deadline versus 'fieldwork substantially complete' on Aug 4. That is a corpus-generation artifact rather than a gold-set defect, but it is the reason founder-q1-02's must_include tier is worth softening.
